status: Rejected after mixed two-pair reference timing. Verified 9e20 app source and assets restored.

decision.decision: reject; no repeatable gain in the two-pair screen
interpretation: Streaming script time per second is nearly flat in pair zero and lower in pair one. The reduction does not repeat at a useful size.
Streaming main-thread task-time rate is mixed and approximately flat; the 20% target remains unmet.
Streaming style and layout time per second increase in both pairs. Normal idle main-thread work also increases in both pairs. Reduced-motion idle work is mixed.
The earlier removal of saved-offset app-store publications is a work-count result and does not override timing.
Do not run a six-pair confirmation or retain this prototype on these preliminary results. Preserve the exact build, patch, source and all seventy rows, then restore verified 9e20 source and assets.
decision.nextAction: Fresh rendering timeline attribution on the restored build, with no speculative gesture-policy or selector changes.
limits: Two pairs on Linux Chromium do not establish device-level confidence or M2 Air gains.
All complete raw attempts and metric rows remain preserved. No failure or adverse metric is removed.

notes: mainThreadMs and mainThreadMsPerSecond use TaskDuration with timeTicks: elapsed time in main-thread tasks, not thread CPU time. Script, style, and layout durations use the same elapsed-time domain.
mainThreadCpuMs uses ThreadTime (renderer main-thread CPU). rendererCpuMs uses ProcessTime (renderer-process CPU); it excludes separate browser, GPU, and backend processes.
Positive reduction means a lower candidate value. Counts such as mounted editors are observations, not optimization scores.
Frame gaps and driver DOM readiness are not INP. Linux CPU throttling is not an M2 Air simulation.

Extra busy headers are backend-seeded status rows, not additional live executions. The six canonical stream producers remain unchanged. Busy-header variants must not be pooled with the default workload.
Final-content probe versions must not be pooled. Locator-assertion retries can collect page-wide ARIA snapshots; boolean polling retains the same visibility gate without those snapshots.

Scripted input variants have a separate mode and window prefix. Their later idle windows can retain composer state changed by those inputs. Action timestamps preserve late execution; they do not imply that all inputs completed on schedule.
Streaming duration includes the wait for final visible content. Fixed-deadline traffic is retained in the raw report.
History decoded bytes include captured requests and responses. They are not compressed network transfer.
